blockers.where: Gotchas {#external-sharing-restrictions} vs the ¹ marks in the Tool inventory
blockers.problem: The gotcha states "Fourteen write tools (marked ¹ in the inventory)" but fifteen tools carry the ¹ mark (copy_file, copy_folder, create_folder, move_file, move_folder, set_file_metadata, set_folder_metadata, update_file_properties, update_folder_properties, upload_file, upload_file_version, create_file_comment, add_items_to_hub, copy_hub, update_hub), and setup.md#external-sharing-restrictions renders the fifteen-tool list.
blockers.suggestion: Re-verify the footnote membership on https://developer.box.com/guides/box-mcp/tools/ and reconcile: fix the stated count to fifteen or correct the erroneous ¹ mark, then propagate any membership change into the tool list in setup.md#external-sharing-restrictions.

blockers.where: remotes[0].tools — the 14 entries with read_only_hint: true (get_download_url through list_docgen_templates)
blockers.problem: meta.yaml asserts read_only_hint: true on 14 tools, but the Dossier's open questions record that whether the live server advertises MCP readOnlyHint annotations is unverifiable and that the Read-only/Write groupings are the documentation's own, and the schema defines read_only_hint as an authored copy of the advertised annotation to omit when the server does not advertise one.
blockers.suggestion: Remove every read_only_hint key from remotes[0].tools; if the hints should stay, first verify the live server's annotations, record that observation in research.md with provenance, and resolve the open question.

blockers.where: #find-box-mcp-server, step 2: "Depending on the console version it is labeled either..."
blockers.problem: The claim that the tile label varies by console version has no backing fact in the Dossier, which records the Box MCP server / Custom Box MCP Server discrepancy as an inconsistency between two documentation pages and an open question, not a version difference.
blockers.suggestion: Drop the causal clause and mirror the Dossier's naming caution, e.g. "The tile may be labeled either **Box MCP server** or **Custom Box MCP Server** — Box's documentation uses both names for the same integration, and both use the configure flow in the next step."

blockers.where: #enable-box-ai-access, step 4: "If required, ensure that you provided consent to the Box AI terms of usage."
blockers.problem: The step is hedged, past-tense narration ("If required... you provided") with no named control, so the careful, literal persona has no action to perform — a direct violation of the second-person imperative, one-action voice rule.
blockers.suggestion: Recast as a conditional imperative within the Dossier fact, e.g. "If Box asks you to consent to the Box AI terms of usage, accept the terms before leaving **Settings**." If the console location of the consent prompt can be verified, name it — that addition would need a Dossier line first.

blockers.where: #set-redirect-uri-and-scopes, step 2 and the paragraph ending "match the options you see in the console to the tool areas your users need."
blockers.problem: The reader must choose scopes with no stated minimum or default, forcing this persona to guess which checkboxes to select for the Speakeasy AI Control Plane connection.
blockers.suggestion: State a concrete floor from the Dossier: select the content scope at minimum (labeled **Content Actions** in Box's earlier developer docs; OAuth scope `root_readwrite`) so the core content tools work, then add the Box AI scope (`ai.readwrite`) only if users need AI tools and the Doc Gen scope (`docgen.readwrite`) only with an Enterprise Advanced license — keeping the existing note that console labels vary.

blockers.where: #copy-client-credentials, paragraph beginning "Box's documentation does not confirm whether the Client Secret remains viewable"
blockers.problem: The guide treats the Client Secret as a possible one-time secret but never says what to do if the reader leaves the page without copying it and it is no longer viewable.
blockers.suggestion: Add a recovery sentence: if you return and the Client Secret is not viewable in the expanded entry, create a new Integration Credentials entry (repeat [Add Integration Credentials](#add-integration-credentials) and [Enter the Redirect URI and select scopes](#set-redirect-uri-and-scopes)) and paste the new Client ID and Client Secret into the Speakeasy AI Control Plane instead.

history.revision_notes: Finding 1 (research, ¹ count): Re-verified footnote membership on https://developer.box.com/guides/box-mcp/tools/ mechanically — fetched the raw HTML and located every <sup>1</sup> marker (WebFetch summaries were inconsistent, so I did not trust them). Exactly fifteen tool names carry the ¹ mark, identical to the Dossier inventory and the setup.md#external-sharing-restrictions list (create_docgen_batch and create_hub are unmarked; the sixteenth <sup> is the footnote definition itself at the page bottom, "Last modified on July 13, 2026" unchanged). Fixed the gotcha in research.md to "Fifteen write tools", corrected the quoted footnote verb to the observed "Only works", and noted the 2026-07-22 re-verification inline. No membership change, so no propagation into setup.md was needed. Finding 2 (meta, read_only_hint): Removed all 14 read_only_hint keys from remotes[0].tools in meta.yaml — the live server's annotations cannot be verified without completing OAuth against Box, so the schema's "omit when the server does not advertise one" rule applies and the Dossier open question stands. Re-validated meta.yaml against schema/guide.v1.schema.json using Python jsonschema (draft-07, FormatChecker, timestamps loaded as strings): SCHEMA VALID; all 54 tool entries carry exactly name+description. (ajv-cli could not run — it rejects the schema's "date-time" format without ajv-formats. An intermediate edit briefly joined some lines; repaired and re-validated before finishing.) Finding 3 (setup, #find-box-mcp-server): Dropped the invented "Depending on the console version" causal clause; step 2 now mirrors the Dossier's naming caution: the tile may be labeled either Box MCP server or Custom Box MCP Server because Box's documentation uses both names for the same integration. Finding 4 (setup, #enable-box-ai-access): Recast step 4 as a conditional imperative: "If Box asks you to consent to the Box AI terms of usage, accept the terms before leaving **Settings**." The console location of the consent prompt remains undocumented, so no control was named. Finding 5 (setup, #set-redirect-uri-and-scopes): Stated a concrete floor — step 2 now says to select the content scope at minimum (labeled Content Actions in Box's earlier developer docs; OAuth scope root_readwrite) so the core content tools work; new steps 3 and 4 add ai.readwrite only if users need Box AI tools and docgen.readwrite only for Doc Gen (Enterprise Advanced license, linked to #plan-gated-tools). Kept the label-variance note as the closing paragraph. All facts trace to the Dossier's scope records. Finding 6 (setup, #copy-client-credentials): First recorded a Recovery line in the Dossier's {#copy-client-credentials} step (derived entirely from recorded facts: Box auto-generates a Client ID and Client Secret per entry, and the add flow is repeatable), then added the recovery sentence to setup.md: if the Client Secret is not viewable on return, create a new Integration Credentials entry (repeat #add-integration-credentials and #set-redirect-uri-and-scopes) and paste the new values into the Speakeasy AI Control Plane. Anchor contract verified: research.md, setup.md, and meta.yaml anchor sets agree; no anchors invented, renamed, or dropped. open_questions: Exact scope checkbox labels in the Integration Credentials UI: docs conflict — 'Access Scopes' with 'Content Actions' (older developer docs), 'Scopes' with 'Manage AI' (support article), 'Select desired Access Scopes' with no labels (current developer docs); mapping of UI labels to OAuth strings root_readwrite / ai.readwrite / docgen.readwrite is undocumented and needs console verification at screenshot capture.
Integration tile label: 'Box MCP server' (developer docs) vs 'Custom Box MCP Server' (support article) for the hover-then-Configure target.

Availability-state option names for integrations are never enumerated ('click the state, then select the state you want to enable'), and whether the Custom Box MCP Server app itself must be set to an enabled state beyond creating Integration Credentials (whose Platform > Platform Apps entry has its own availability) is undocumented.
Whether the Client Secret remains viewable on later visits to the expanded credential entry or is effectively shown once — the documented flow implies it stays viewable but no source confirms it.

Whether the live server advertises MCP readOnlyHint annotations — hints in meta.yaml derive from the documentation's Read-only/Write groupings, not a live tools/list; who_am_i, Search, and Box AI tools are ungrouped in the docs and carry no hint.
Default tool-enablement state for a newly enabled enterprise in the Box MCP Server tool-access tab (beyond the four external-sharing tools documented 'Off by default').

How the reader reaches the Admin Console from app.box.com is not recorded (provider docs start inside it); step 2 of {#open-integrations} says only "Open the Admin Console" with no named control — needs capture-time verification.

Exact scope checkbox labels in the credential entry, and their mapping to root_readwrite / ai.readwrite / docgen.readwrite, are undocumented (Dossier open question); the guide shows both documented label variants (Content Actions, Manage AI) and tells the reader to match by tool area.
Integration tile label is documented inconsistently (Box MCP server vs Custom Box MCP Server); rendered as either/or pending console verification.
Whether the Client Secret remains viewable on return visits is unconfirmed; rendered as a pre-step warning to copy immediately.

Whether the Custom Box MCP Server app must be set to an enabled availability state beyond creating Integration Credentials is undocumented; the guide includes no availability-state step (the prior stale draft had invented one).

Dossier-internal discrepancy: the {#external-sharing-restrictions} gotcha says "Fourteen write tools" but the tool inventory marks 15 tools with the footnote; setup.md lists the 15 marked tools without asserting a count — the Dossier should reconcile the number.
